lab-hidden-file.title: Own exercise: hidden file
lab-hidden-file.objective: In a folder full of ordinary files, a flag sits in a file you can't see with a plain ls. Find it using the terminal.
hints: Files and folders starting with a dot are hidden by default.
Look at the options for ls, and remember that hidden folders can contain hidden files.

lab-log-secret.title: Own exercise: secret in a log
lab-log-secret.objective: A log file with thousands of lines accidentally includes a secret. Find it without reading the whole log.
hints: You're looking for one line that stands out. Don't read everything.
grep -i with words like token, secret, key, or the flag's format.

lab-env-leak.title: Own exercise: secret in environment variables
lab-env-leak.objective: Start the service with the lab's script. The secret exists only as an environment variable in the running process. Find it from another terminal.
hints: Find the process ID first (ps, pgrep).
Linux exposes each process's environment under /proc/<pid>/.

lab-modbus-flag.title: Own exercise: flag in Modbus traffic
lab-modbus-flag.objective: You get a small PCAP with Modbus/TCP traffic between a client and a device (synthetic test addresses only). Someone writes a flag to the device. Find it.
hints: Start with the display filter modbus in Wireshark.
Some things are read, some are written. Which function codes write?
Register values are just numbers. What could two bytes per register represent?

ics-fc-quiz.title: Modbus function codes from memory
ics-fc-quiz.objective: Without looking anything up: write what function codes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 15 and 16 do, and which ones read and which write. Then check against the traffic in the Modbus exercise and note what you got wrong.
hints: The function codes are split into coils (1 bit) and registers (16 bit).
There are two read codes and two write codes for each of the two types.

ics-wireshark-filters.title: Wireshark filters for Modbus from memory
ics-wireshark-filters.objective: Write filters from memory for: Modbus writes only, a single unit ID only, and requests from one given IP only. Test them against the exercise PCAP.
hints: Field names start with modbus. Use 'Apply as Filter' on a field to see its name.
Combine with && and ip.src == .

labex-hidden-file.title: Hidden File Hunt
labex-hidden-file.objective: Find a flag hidden in a directory structure, using only the terminal.
hints: A dot at the start of the name hides a file.
Look at the options for ls.

labex-weak-password.title: Weak Password Access
labex-weak-password.objective: Gain access to a local test account in the lab that has a weak password, and find the flag. Lab environment only.
hints: Which passwords do people choose most often?
A small wordlist and one shell are enough.

labex-open-port.title: Open Port Discovery
labex-open-port.objective: Find a local TCP service that is listening, and fetch the flag from it.
hints: ss -tln shows listening ports.
curl or nc can talk to the service.

labex-exposed-backup.title: Audit and Repair an Exposed Backup
labex-exposed-backup.objective: Find a backup with overly open permissions, and fix them so only the owner has access.
hints: ls -l shows who can read and write.
chmod can use octal numbers, for example for owner-only.

labex-log-secret.title: Log File Secret
labex-log-secret.objective: Find a secret that was logged by mistake.
hints: grep is the tool.
Search for words like secret, token, password.

labex-dir-traversal.title: Basic Directory Traversal
labex-dir-traversal.objective: Explain in your own words why ../ can read a file outside the intended directory, and show it in the lab.
hints: What does .. mean in a path?
Why does the program trust the path you give it?

labex-env-leak.title: Environment Variable Leak
labex-env-leak.objective: Find a secret exposed as an environment variable.
hints: env and printenv.
Different shells can have different variables.

labex-script-analysis.title: Simple Script Analysis
labex-script-analysis.objective: Read a bash script and work out what it generates when run, without guessing.
hints: Read first, run afterwards, and only in the lab.
Look for variables and command substitution.

labex-network-service.title: Network Service Exploit
labex-network-service.objective: Fetch the flag from a simple local network service in the lab.
hints: Find the port first.
nc sends and receives raw text.

labex-web-input.title: Basic Web Input Vulnerability
labex-web-input.objective: Send a simple POST request to a local form in the lab and get the flag.
hints: Look at the form's fields in the source code.
curl -d 'field=value' URL.
